q: A question describes a real requirement attached to the wrong provision. Which of the following is such a case?
options: A census condition attached to the operation of women's reservation in panchayats
A census condition attached to the operation of the 2023 reservation amendment
A written Cabinet advice requirement attached to a Proclamation of Emergency
A fourteen-day period attached to the return of a Money Bill by the upper House
expl: The census condition belongs to the 2023 amendment, not to local body reservation.
why: Three options state requirements correctly attached; only one transplants a condition across provisions.
trapnote: Requirements travel badly. A condition attached to one amendment rarely applies to another.

q: Consider: 1-A directive becomes enforceable when read into a Fundamental Right. 2-A Fundamental Duty becomes enforceable when a statute gives it effect. 3-Both are directly enforceable by writ. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Neither is directly enforceable; each operates through a different route.
why: The two routes differ: one runs through a right and the other through a statute.
trapnote: Two indirect routes: a directive through a right, a duty through a statute.

q: Which combination correctly describes the current position on reservation?
options: The ceiling binds all reservation, including the economic quota
The ceiling has been abolished and no limit now operates on any reservation
The ceiling binds backward-class reservation; the economic quota sits outside it
The ceiling binds the economic quota; backward-class reservation sits outside it
expl: The ceiling was confined rather than abolished, and the economic quota was placed outside it.
why: The fourth option reverses the two compartments, which is a cleaner error than a candidate expects.
trapnote: Confined, not abolished. The compartment it binds is the backward-class compartment.

q: A fact-pattern involves an illegal detention, a denial of legal aid and a refusal of admission to an aided school. Which statement is correct?
options: Three Directive Principles are engaged, none directly enforceable by writ
Three separate provisions are engaged, only one of which is a Directive Principle
Three Fundamental Rights are engaged, each enforceable in the Supreme Court
Only the detention is justiciable, the remaining limbs being matters of policy
expl: Liberty and admission-equality are rights; legal aid is a directive read into a right.
why: Uniform characterisation of a multi-limb fact-pattern is almost always the wrong answer.
trapnote: Multi-limb patterns rarely share one category. Classify each limb before answering.

q: Consider the following on the amending power: 1-Parliament may amend any provision. 2-It may not damage the basic structure. 3-Procedural compliance cures a basic-structure defect. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Procedural compliance and the substantive limit are independent of each other.
why: A measure may satisfy every procedural requirement and still fall on the substantive limit.
trapnote: Two independent checks. Satisfying one says nothing about the other.

q: Which statement correctly identifies the distinction between two remedies?
options: Prohibition quashes an order already made; certiorari restrains pending proceedings
Both restrain pending proceedings, differing only in the court that issues them
Both quash orders already made, differing only in the authority addressed
Prohibition restrains proceedings that are pending; certiorari quashes an order already made
expl: The distinction is one of timing.
why: The pair is the most frequently reversed in the whole of the remedies topic.
trapnote: Prohibition prevents; certiorari cures. The distinction is timing, not court or authority.

q: Consider a set of options in which two are defensible and one is more complete. Which approach is correct?
options: Select the option that is shortest and therefore least likely to contain an error
Select the option that most closely repeats the language of the stem
Select the option that accounts for every limb of the stem
Select the option that names the most authorities, being most comprehensive
expl: Completeness against the stem is the criterion, not length or vocabulary.
why: The remaining options describe surface heuristics that a well-constructed paper defeats.
trapnote: Answer against the stem, limb by limb. Surface features are engineered to mislead.

q: Consider: 1-The abolition of untouchability binds private persons. 2-The general equality guarantee binds private persons. 3-The prohibition of child labour binds private persons. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The general equality guarantee binds the State alone.
why: Two of the horizontal provisions are correctly stated and the vertical one is placed between them.
trapnote: The general guarantee is vertical. The specific ones beside it are horizontal.

q: A candidate must choose between two options that differ only in the year stated. Which approach is correct?
options: Anchor the event to a neighbouring event whose date is certain and reason from it
Select the earlier year, amendments generally being older than they appear
Select the later year, constitutional change having accelerated over time
Select the year that matches the number of the amendment concerned
expl: Relative dating from a fixed anchor is more reliable than recall of an isolated year.
why: The remaining options describe guessing strategies that have no foundation.
trapnote: Date relatively, not absolutely. Anchor to an event you are certain of and work outwards.

q: Which statement correctly summarises the treatment of a superseded position offered as current law?
options: It is a correct option if it accurately states the historical position
It is a correct option where the stem does not specify a date
It is a wrong option only where the change occurred within the last decade
It is a wrong option, however accurately it states what the law once was
expl: An option must state the law as it stands unless the stem asks otherwise.
why: The third option is the most tempting, because stems frequently omit an express date.
trapnote: Absent words to the contrary, a stem asks for the present position.
